stem:
Avni invests $\mathrm{Rs}\,8000$ at $5\%$ per year, compounded annually, for $2$ years.

Which claim correctly gives the amount after $2$ years?

options.text: Each year adds $\mathrm{Rs}\,400$ on the original $\mathrm{Rs}\,8000$ only, so the amount is $\mathrm{Rs}\,8800$.
Compounding also covers interest paid out each year with the principal kept fixed at $\mathrm{Rs}\,8000$.
After year $1$ the amount is $\mathrm{Rs}\,8400$; year $2$ interest on $\mathrm{Rs}\,8400$ gives amount $\mathrm{Rs}\,8820$.
The amount is $5\%$, the printed rate.

teacher.key_rationale: Compound interest updates the base: 8000→8400 after year 1, then 5% of 8400 gives 8820. Keeping the principal fixed is simple interest. Reading only the printed rate is a surface grab.
